Processing video at 1 FPS is officially dead weight for large language models.

As developers, we are seeing a massive shift in how models interact with complex data formats, from video files to 3D environments and physical hardware.

Here are the key technical updates from the last 24 hours:

🎥 Google launched Agentic Video Understanding for Gemini Flash models, cutting video tokens by up to 88% by navigating video to load only the required segments instead of ingesting at 1 FPS.

🏠 Claude Fable 5.1 has shown it can build a full 3D house in Blender from a single prompt, demonstrating new capabilities in programmatic asset generation.

💻 A new NInfer fork introduces a 555k context at fp4 for the Nvidia 5090, featuring a custom NVFP4 KV cache built from scratch for QIn3.8-27B using a custom MMA kernel.

🤖 Integrations of GPT-6 Astra on robot arms have surfaced, highlighting the ongoing push toward embodied artificial intelligence.

We are moving away from brute-force token ingestion and toward highly targeted, agentic data retrieval. Optimizing the KV cache and leveraging agentic navigation are becoming essential strategies as we build more complex, context-heavy applications. This will drastically lower API costs and compute requirements for production apps.

Which of these approaches to token reduction and efficiency are you planning to test in your own workflow this week?
